articles.title: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
articles.summary:
Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This difficult decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement.
Quad9’s departure from France is both disheartening and understandable. The court’s ruling put the organization in the impossible bind of having to choose between crippling litigation and penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing the exit door instead.
The withdrawal of a basic infrastructure service from France fundamentally harms the free and open Internet, and it should serve as a warning of the damage that will result if rightsholders and policymakers continue demanding maximal blocking across every layer of the Internet. It not only deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy and important tool; it creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives. Quad9’s resolver is used by a wide variety of individuals and organizations in France — including government bodies, educational institutions, hospitals, and utilities — and Quad9 has no way to directly notify those individuals and institutions that their resolver will soon stop working. Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free

US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.
Google first introduced its Spark AI agent in May, but it was only available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. The launch of tasks in Gemini brings Spark’s capabilities to all users in the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India. You can find tasks by opening Gemini and changing the toggle on the homepage from “Chat” to “Tasks.”

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Optimizely Vulnerability Exploited to Serve Malware on Major Websites
articles.summary:
Digital experience platform Optimizely has patched a vulnerability that hackers exploited to inject malicious code into customer projects, causing the websites of many major organizations to serve malware to visitors.
The company confirmed the incident in a status page update posted early on November 17 and in a post on X, where it said some Web Experimentation customers were affected.
“Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects,” the company said on its status page. “We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.”
Optimizely added that it has taken steps to secure affected user accounts and introduced additional protections, but it has not said how many customers were impacted.
Report URI, a security firm that investigated the attack, said it examined 1,611 Optimizely scripts and identified 188 infected ones, belonging to 178 organizations. Names on the list include the BBC, CNN, Zoom, GitLab, Salesforce, Equifax, HSBC and IKEA.
According to Report URI, the malicious code was placed in an optional field meant for a customer’s own JavaScript, which executes on every page. The tampered files came from Optimizely’s content delivery network, so the websites loading them treated them as trusted.

articles.title: Voyager 1 atteint un jour-lumière de la Terre : à 26 milliards de km de la Terre, cela aurait pris 28 250 ans en voiture
articles.summary:
Lorsque vient le moment d’appréhender les distances absolument colossales dans l’univers, la mesure de référence est l’année-lumière. C’est elle qui permet usuellement d’indiquer l’écart entre des objets incroyablement distants entre eux. Et c’est parfois presque insuffisant, à l’image de ce signal ayant franchi 10 milliards d’années-lumière avant de nous parvenir.
La notion d’année-lumière est en fait assez simple à comprendre : cette unité de longueur détermine la distance parcourue par la lumière dans le vide en un an. Du coup, on saisit facilement la logique d’un jour-lumière. C’est la même chose, mais en 24 heures. Mais concrètement, à quoi cela correspond-il ?
Cette question se pose avec force, car le jour-lumière est aujourd’hui au cœur de l’actualité : en effet, ce 18 novembre, vers 11h16 (heure de Paris), la sonde Voyager 1 de la NASA franchira cette barre d’un jour-lumière de distance avec la Terre. Aucun autre objet fabriqué par l’humanité n’est allé aussi loin : Voyager 1 détient ce record depuis février 1998, quand elle a dépassé la sonde Pioneer 10. Jusqu’ici, on comptait sa distance en heures-lumière.
En 24 heures, donc, la lumière traverse dans le vide la distance de 25,9 milliards de kilomètres. La conséquence ? Une instruction envoyée par radio depuis la Terre met une journée entière pour atteindre la sonde. Sa réponse met autant de temps à revenir. Un échange simple prend donc deux longues journées. Et ça ne va faire que s’aggraver.

articles.title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
articles.summary:
Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
Discover how we built the open Agent Host Protocol to keep your agent sessions accessible across editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.
Models are now good enough to work for hours or even days on their own. You don’t have to watch over every thing they do, but you still need to be able to check in, no matter where you are. An agent can’t live only inside one application. The work should continue even If you close a window or switch devices.
In GitHub Copilot you can start an agent session in one place and pick it up in another. This session continuity runs on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), an open standard built first in VS Code and adopted across GitHub. Here’s how it works, what we learned building it, and how you can use it to bring your agents into your own apps and workflows.
Why one integration per client stopped working
GitHub Copilot was first built in VS Code as an extension that bundled its own harness. This gave you access to your agents in VS Code, but it tied their lifetime to the editor. Extensions are attached to a single VS Code window. Close that window, and the agent is gone. Update VS Code, and every agent stops as the application restarts. Connect to a remote machine, and you get an entirely new extension host commit-locked against the version of the VS Code workbench you have.

articles.title: AI Is Giving Optical Computing Another Shot
articles.summary:
AI Is Giving Optical Computing Another Shot
The push to cut AI inference’s energy use could pay off in unexpected ways
The idea of computing with light has been around for over 70 years, but until recently it’s remained largely in the realm of research. Over the past few years, though, optical computing has emerged as a fast-growing industry: Market valuation of companies in this sector now totals US $2.22 billion, up from $0.4 billion in 2022. One projection suggests that the market will continue to grow exponentially in the coming years.
The reason for this sudden surge will surprise no one: AI. In particular, AI inference—the process of using AI models to respond to user queries—has driven much of the construction of huge, power-hungry data centers, and relatively energy-efficient optical systems are seen as a potential way forward.
“Most of the interest in [photonics] is driven by the fact that AI inference has literally become limited by power, and in a rather striking manner,” says Peter McMahon, associate professor of applied and engineering physics at Cornell University, in Ithaca, N.Y., who has researched optical computing for over a decade.
Optics, at least on paper, carries the promise of doing the same math as today’s GPUs at a drastically lower level of power. Switching from electronics to optics would be a pretty radical solution. Nevertheless, like mushrooms after a rainstorm, optical-computing startups are popping up in the United States, China, Germany, and I…

Kleinere Teams, weniger Freigaben, neue Rollen: Wie Unternehmen ihre Organisation für KI umbauen müssen
Ein Chatbot hier, ein Copilot dort: In den meisten Unternehmen gehört Künstliche Intelligenz zum Alltag, allerdings meist als Werkzeug für einzelne Aufgaben. Wie groß die Lücke zwischen Nutzung und echtem Umbau ist, zeigt eine Befragung der Technologieberatung Bearing Point. Demnach ist KI nur bei acht Prozent der deutschen Unternehmen tief in die meisten Geschäftsabläufe integriert und liefert messbare Erfolge. In China liegt der Anteil bei 20 Prozent, in den USA bei 18 Prozent.
Unser Cover bringt auf den Punkt, worum es jetzt geht: Aus der GmbH & Co. KG wird die GmbH & Co. KI. Solange KI nur ein Tool unter vielen ist, bleibt ihr Effekt begrenzt. Sie muss ein grundlegender Teil der Organisation werden. Der Organisationsforscher Kai Reinhardt von der HTW Berlin formuliert es so: „Viele betrachten KI fälschlicherweise als Softwaretool und nicht als Infrastruktur, die neue Prozesse und Entscheidungswege eröffnet.“
Wie das konkret aussehen kann, zeigen die Unternehmen in unserer Titelstrecke. Beim Auto-Abo-Anbieter Finn entsteht ein Großteil des Codes inzwischen automatisiert. articles.title: Maintainers don't need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
articles.summary:
Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half.
AI has made finding potential vulnerabilities fast and cheap. Fixing them still takes human judgment, and in open source, that work falls to maintainers. Many are already flooded with AI-generated security findings, including duplicates and reports that aren’t vulnerabilities at all. Another raw scan doesn’t help them. Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings.
AI shouldn’t add to maintainers’ workload. So, with maintainers, GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot together: could AI help maintainers ship fixes instead of handing them more findings?
GitHub and Microsoft are using Codename MDASH, Microsoft’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, to find and fix security vulnerabilities in widely used open source software, strengthening the foundation that much of the world’s code is built on.
The process
Our pilot had two goals: send only findings that matter, and never send a maintainer an unverified finding. Here’s how it worked:
Find.Codename MDASH, an AI system from Microsoft Security, scanned each project using Microsoft’s MAI Cyber model and suggested fixes for what it found.

Hodak announced that the device is now being trialed for patients with another blindness-causing condition, Stargardt disease, while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.
With the funding, the company aims to bring the device to the United States through the FDA’s Humanitarian Device Exemption, which lets experimental medical technology be used to treat rare conditions. articles.title: IEEE Celebrates 10 Years of Incorporating Ethics Into AI Systems
articles.summary:
Policymakers, technologists, and members of the public have raised concerns about the harm AI’s rapid advancement might cause to society. Their concerns include bias, data privacy violations, the spread of misinformation, and losing control of AI agents.
Those issues are relatively new to many people, but the IEEE Standards Association has been working for the past decade on ways to prioritize the responsible development of AI systems.
In 2016 IEEE SA launched the IEEE Global Initiative for Ethical Considerations in Autonomous and Intelligent Systems (A/IS) and published the Ethically Aligned Design report. EAD’s mission is to encourage everyone involved in designing autonomous and intelligent systems to prioritize human well-being by applying ethical considerations for the benefit of humanity.
Developed by a multidisciplinary community of experts from around the world, the report outlined eight foundational principles for A/IS. They include human rights, people’s well-being, and transparency. More than 100 leading AI ethics experts provided input. EAD’s Version II report was released in 2017. Both versions solicited public input and received hundreds of pages of feedback, according to John C. Havens, who was the global initiative’s founding executive director, and is now the global director for IEEE Planet Positive 2030. And by 2019, there were more than 400 contributors and the community continues to grow.

articles.title: COP 31: Auch die Weltklimakonferenz geht die Umweltfolgen des KI-Booms nicht an
articles.summary:
COP 31: Auch die Weltklimakonferenz geht die Umweltfolgen des KI-Booms nicht an
Sowohl Schätzungen der Internationalen Energieagentur als auch der Vereinten Nationen kommen zu dem Schluss, dass sich der Energieverbrauch durch Rechenzentren in der Zeit von 2025 bis 2030 verdoppeln wird – vor allem wegen der steigenden KI‑Nutzung. Im Angesicht dieses massiv steigenden Energieverbrauchs sollte man sich eigentlich freuen, dass das Thema auch bei der noch bis zum 20. November 2026 laufenden Weltklimakonferenz COP 31 in Antalya zur Sprache kommt.
Eigentlich – denn was die türkisch-australische COP-31-Präsidentschaft zu dem Thema vorgelegt hat, eignet sich nicht im Geringsten, um den Auswirkungen des KI-Booms auf die Umwelt gerecht zu werden. Dabei klingt es ja eigentlich nicht schlecht. Immerhin erklären die Unterzeichner des Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge „ihr gemeinsames Ziel, KI zu einem Teil der Klimalösung zu machen“. Und zwar indem sie „nachhaltig betrieben, effizient konzipiert, transparent gemessen und für alle zugänglich“ wird.

articles.summary:
California’s attorney general filed a lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday in an effort to force the ChatGPT-maker to change its business practices over a July cybersecurity incident in which its artificial intelligence system hacked into another company on its own.
In the lawsuit filed in San Francisco Superior Court, Attorney General Rob Bonta alleges that OpenAI misled and endangered the public and users of its services by knowingly developing advanced AI models without necessary safeguards. He says the company’s actions could put critical infrastructure, institutions and the public at risk, which makes it a “public nuisance” under state law. Bonta says OpenAI is a public nuisance, and he wants a judge to order the company to change its ways and give up any profits generated by what he claims are the company’s risky business practices.
OpenAI announced an “unprecedented cyber incident ” on July 21, when its AI agent hacked into another AI company, Hugging Face, after escaping from what was supposed to be an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox. OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face’s servers.
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that has been identified by every major AI lab.

articles.title: Google Maps change radicalement : Gemini peut organiser vos vacances et prendre vos rendez-vous
articles.summary:
Google Maps vient d’être enrichi d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité baptisée « Demander à Maps ». Il serait question de « la plus grande mise à jour de Google Maps depuis plus de dix ans », selon Google. Le principe est simple : Gemini est intégré à Google Maps pour vous aider à planifier vos vacances, réserver vos plats ou encore prendre des rendez-vous à votre place. Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir.
Gemini se transforme en guide de voyage
La fonctionnalité « Demander à Maps » se présente sous la forme d’une fenêtre conversationnelle disponible aussi bien sur le web que sur l’application Google Maps. Google précise que cette fonctionnalité est basée sur les données de plus de 300 millions de lieux et sur les avis de plus de 500 millions de contributeurs.

articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.summary:
Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
- Date:
- November 11, 2026
- Source:
- ETH Zurich
- Summary:
- Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.

articles.title: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people
articles.summary:
Ride-hailing company Uber is notifying nearly 150,000 drivers that attackers stole their data after breaching AI infrastructure provider Fireworks in early October.
In breach notification letters sent to affected individuals on November 10, Uber said threat actors accessed their personal information after breaching an Uber account with a third-party service provider.
While Uber didn't share the total number of affected drivers in these letters, it revealed in a filing with Maine's Office of the Attorney General that the data breach has exposed the information of 149,346 drivers, including their names, driver’s license numbers, dates of birth, and addresses.
After being informed of the breach, Uber launched an investigation and severed data connections with the service provider to block further malicious access to its data.
"On October 9, 2026, a service provider notified Uber that an unauthorized third party had compromised the service provider's internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account with the service provider," Uber said. "After being notified of this incident, Uber immediately severed data connections with the service provider and launched an investigation. On October 13, 2026, our investigation determined that the unauthorized party had used the compromised credentials to access Uber data connected to the service provider."

articles.title: James Bond : tapez Robert Pattinson sur Google
articles.summary:
Plus de 5 ans après Mourir peut attendre, le dernier film James Bond mettant en vedette Daniel Craig, Amazon MGM Studios a enfin officialisé le nom du nouveau 007 ce lundi 16 novembre : Robert Pattinson, préféré aux autres finalistes du casting. Depuis, tout est commenté, des qualités de Robert Pattinson pour le rôle, jusqu’à la position de son doigt sur la première image officielle où il incarne James Bond.
Google s’y est mis aussi, avec un easter egg, une de ces animations cachées que le moteur de recherche lance sur certaines requêtes. Comme l’a repéré le média NDTV Profit ce 17 novembre, une recherche « Robert Pattinson » fait trembler la page de résultats, puis des zestes de citron tombent sur l’écran.
Pourquoi un citron quand on cherche « Robert Pattison » dans Google ?
La réponse est dans le verre de James Bond. La page qui tremble rappelle sa commande fétiche, un martini « shaken, not stirred », c’est-à-dire préparé au shaker plutôt qu’à la cuillère. Le citron remonte encore plus loin, à Casino Royale, le roman de 1953 dans lequel Ian Fleming crée l’agent secret. Bond y invente le Vesper, un mélange de gin, de vodka et de Kina Lillet (un apéritif français), secoué jusqu’à être glacé, puis servi avec une grande et fine tranche d’écorce de citron.
Le magazine The Hollywood Reporter résume l’animation à sa façon : les photos de l’acteur sont servies secouées, avec un zeste de citron.

articles.title: Microsoft aclara uno de los mayores misterios de Windows cuando el rendimiento se desploma
articles.summary:
Microsoft ha explicado por qué el truco más obvio para acelerar Windows no funciona. Cuando el sistema operativo se vuelve lento o deja de responder, muchos recurren al Administrador de tareas para identificar el problema y cerrar el proceso responsable. No obstante, existen situaciones en donde el propio Administrador y la barra de tareas dejan de responder cuando más se necesitan.
Debido a ello, muchos se preguntan por qué Microsoft no asigna una prioridad más alta a estos procesos. Al ejecutarse con más privilegios, seguirían funcionando sin problemas, incluso cuando el procesador se satura y el ordenador deja de responder. Lamentablemente para los usuarios de Windows, el problema es más complejo de lo que parece y un cambio de prioridades no lo resolvería.
Raymond Chen, un ingeniero veterano de Microsoft que fue pieza clave de Windows 95 y el desarrollo de la interfaz de usuario, reveló que aumentar la prioridad de un proceso permite que obtenga tiempo de CPU antes que otros procesos menos importantes. El problema es que esto no siempre funciona, ya que el problema aparece cuando una aplicación se acaba los recursos compartidos.
Según Chen, tener prioridad alta es como tener un pase preferente en la fila del supermercado. Puedes avanzar hasta el frente más rápido que los demás clientes, pero si la persona que está siendo atendida tiene un carrito lleno de productos, tendrás que esperar a que termine.

articles.title: La empresa de fotos de autos EVOX demandó a ByteDance por usar 7.095 imágenes para entrenar su IA
articles.summary:
EVOX Productions, una empresa californiana de fotografía automotriz, demandó a ByteDance, la dueña de TikTok, por copyright. Sostiene que ByteDance copió 7.095 de sus fotos sin permiso y las usó para entrenar Seedream, su generador de imágenes con inteligencia artificial (IA), según la denuncia presentada el 29 de octubre de 2026.
El caso tramita en el Tribunal de Distrito para el Distrito Central de California, con el número 5:26-cv-06428. Los acusados son ByteDance Inc. y ByteDance Ltd. La denuncia plantea dos cargos: infracción directa de derechos de autor e infracción contributiva, es decir, responsabilidad por lo que hagan los usuarios de Seedream.
EVOX afirma que tiene más de dos millones de fotografías protegidas y que invirtió unos USD 56 millones en su biblioteca durante tres décadas. Vende licencias a empresas del sector automotor y, por imagen, a través del sitio EvoxStock.com.
Una descarga detectada en abril
Según la denuncia, el 10 de abril de 2026 una revisión de los registros de sus servidores mostró que ByteDance había entrado sin autorización a EvoxStock.com y copiado las 7.095 imágenes. Un anexo de unas 100 páginas las lista junto con sus números de registro de derechos de autor.

articles.title: Coup dur pour Audi : la très attendue berline électrique est repoussée à 2029

Audi en retard ? Oh, jamais de la vie ! Pour preuve, la marque avait prévu le coup en annonçant une A4 électrique il y a maintenant quatre ans, histoire de tailler des croupières à la Tesla Model 3. BMW et Mercedes avaient aussi des plans similaires dans les cartons, sans encore avancer quoi que ce soit à l’époque. Les anneaux avaient donc une belle avance. Hélas, les années sont passées sans grandes nouvelles.
Et les deux grands rivaux ont dégainé entre temps les i4, i3 et Classe C sans aucune réaction de la part d’Audi. Pire encore, il s’avère que les modèles précités sont d’indéniables réussites. Où est donc passée l’A4 électrique ? Aux oubliettes ? Non, bien heureusement, mais il faudra en revanche se montrer patient pour espérer la découvrir. D’après Autocar, la berline devrait débarquer d’ici… 2029. On voit déjà BMW et Mercedes sabrer le champagne.
Problèmes financiers et plateforme inédite : les raisons de la douche froide
Quelle est donc la raison d’un tel retard ? Audi a voulu faire les choses bien avec une plateforme inédite, la Scalable Systems, pour armer au mieux son modèle. Sauf que les problèmes financiers traversés par le groupe Volkswagen ont sérieusement contrecarré les plans de la marque. articles.title: Can AI help build a healthier future? - Microsoft Research
articles.summary:
Technical advancement is moving at such a rapid pace that it can be challenging to define the tomorrow we’re working toward. In The Shape of Things to Come, Microsoft Research leader Doug Burger and experts from across disciplines tease out the thorniest AI issues facing technologists, policymakers, business decisionmakers, and other stakeholders today. The goal: to amplify the shared understanding needed to build a future in which the AI transition is a net positive.
Microsoft Principal Research Manager Ava Amini, Microsoft Chief Scientific Officer Eric Horvitz, and physician-scientist and Microsoft AI health advisor Eric Topol (opens in new tab) of Scripps Research join Burger to tackle a question with ramifications for every individual on the planet: What might the future of medicine look like with AI, and what needs to happen first?
Drawing from experiences in machine learning, bioscience, and clinical care, the group explores AI-assisted medical diagnosis, the untapped potential of leveraging AI in medical imaging, whole-patient models, virtual cells, and the role of biological foundation models in scientific discovery. The group also examines why promising research can be slow to reach patients, how AI could guide experiments and drug discovery, and why better biological data and real-world validation remain essential.

articles.title: 1998 KY26: Warum ein Asteroid plötzlich die Wissenschaft verblüfft
articles.summary:
Physik-Rätsel im All: Warum Asteroid 1998 KY26 plötzlich beschleunigt
Der erdnahe Asteroid mit der Bezeichnung 1998 KY26 bewegt sich nicht allein nach den Gesetzen der Schwerkraft durch das All, sondern erfährt senkrecht zu seiner Umlaufbahn um die Sonne eine zusätzliche, sogenannte nichtgravitative Beschleunigung. Bislang vermuteten mehrere Wissenschaftler:innen hinter dieser Bahnabweichung unsichtbar verdampfendes Wassereis im Inneren des Himmelskörpers, doch wie in einer im Fachmagazin Icarus veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, erweist sich der Gesteinsbrocken für dauerhafte Eisvorräte als deutlich zu warm.
Für die Untersuchung haben die beiden Raumfahrtingenieure Korbin Hansen und Masatoshi Hirabayashi vom Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta im US-Bundesstaat Georgia ein dreidimensionales Computermodell eingesetzt, das die Wärmeleitung von der Oberfläche bis in den Kern des rund elf Meter großen Körpers berechnet. Ihren Simulationen zufolge liegt die Temperatur selbst an den kältesten Stellen im Durchschnitt eines Sonnenumlaufs bei mindestens 212 Kelvin, was minus 61 Grad Celsius entspricht, während Wassereis im Vakuum selbst unter einer schützenden Gesteinsschicht nur unterhalb von 145 Kelvin beziehungsweise minus 128 Grad Celsius über längere Zeiträume stabil bleibt.

What we know so far: The FBI says that hackers are using an AI-driven penetration testing tool called Artex to automate attacks that used to require skilled human operators. The software connects to large language models and handles the scanning, exploitation and lateral movement on its own, and in some cases it has gone from first targeting a system to active compromise "in under three hours."
Artex belongs to a growing category of open-source AI penetration testing platforms. Victims linked to the tool so far include IT management firm ConnectWise and thousands of its customers, security vendor Barracuda, and a group of South Korean financial institutions.
Security teams use this kind of software to probe their own defenses before attackers do the same. The FBI says attackers have taken the same capability and turned it outward against financial services firms, government agencies, technology and defense companies, telecom and internet providers, and law firms.
The tool's design explains much of its appeal. Operators can connect Artex to hosted frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI, open-source models, or models built outside the US. Once connected, Artex usually begins by scanning a target network quickly for weak spots. It then goes after simple flaws, such as poor protections and exposed or stolen passwords, to get an initial foothold. From there it moves toward databases, mailboxes and other stores of sensitive information.

The startup trains frontier foundation models and deploys them as AI agents alongside existing security tools to audit security data and correlate signals across environments to improve defenses and help security teams respond to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks.

articles.title: Las leónidas pueden ser la mejor lluvia de estrellas del año o la más decepcionante. Esta noche toca lo segundo
articles.summary:
Si pensamos en una lluvia de estrellas abundante, en el hemisferio norte seguro que nos vienen a la mente las perseidas. En el sur son más de gemínidas, porque tienen lugar cuando allí es verano, como pasa con las perseidas en el norte. Ambas suelen regalarnos espectáculos de más de 100 meteoros por hora, muy agradables de ver. También hay otras igual de potentes, como las cuadrántidas.
Más allá de eso, la mayoría de lluvias de estrellas suelen pasar desapercibidas. Sin embargo, hay algunas que normalmente pasan sin pena ni gloria, pero que en algunos momentos de la historia superaron con creces a perseidas y gemínidas. Es el caso de las leónidas, que en 1966 dieron lugar a una tormenta de más de 144.000 meteoros por hora. Esta noche será el pico de esta lluvia de estrellas. ¿Qué podemos esperar de ellas?
Más estrellas de las que se pueden contar. En 1966, el científico jefe del planetario Hayden de Nueva York, Kenneth L. Franklin, calculó que la noche del 17 de noviembre tendría lugar la lluvia de estrellas más abundante que ningún humano vivo hubiese visto jamás. Según sus predicciones, las leónidas bombardearían el cielo, superando los 100.000 meteoros por hora. Tal fue su emoción que animó a todo el mundo a acudir a Central Park para tumbarse en el césped y disfrutar del espectáculo. Y también importa si el bajón se nota sólo con el agua caliente o en todo.
La cal del aireador. Cuando el culpable es un único grifo, lo más probable es que la pieza que tiene en la boca, el aireador, se haya ido llenando de cal y otras partículas. articles.title: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
articles.summary:
Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them.
Named Remote Lock, this new feature is shipping to devices upgraded to Windows 11 Insider Preview builds in the Beta (Build 26320.10003) and Experimental (Build 26340.10013) channels.
Admins can use Microsoft Intune custom configuration profiles to lock Microsoft Entra-joined, hybrid-joined, or MDM-enrolled devices that run Windows Enterprise, Education, or Pro.
After the IT department remotely locks the device, the system can only be unlocked via Intune, since PINs, passwords, local admins, or web sign-ins will no longer work. Microsoft added that the user's credentials will remain valid and can still be used to sign into other devices that haven't been locked.
"Windows signs out every active session, hides all sign-in options and shows a locked screen," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines. "Nothing is erased: the device stays enrolled and managed, BitLocker stays on and user data stays in place. The lock holds across restarts and while offline, and only an admin can lift it remotely, so the user picks up where they left off."
Admins can lock a device from the Intune admin center using the following procedure:
- Go to Devices > Windows > Configuration > Create > New policy. Choose Windows 10 and later, then Templates > Custom.

Changing weights won’t fix a failure elsewhere in the system. When the model is the right place to intervene, production evidence can improve both quality and economics. A smaller model might reproduce a more expensive model’s behavior; better examples might improve consistency; an outcome-based reward might suit the task. Refining a capable model can also avoid another migration to a new model generation.

National programs in North America, Europe, and Asia are driving the installation of quantum processing units (QPUs) alongside high-performance computing (HPC) systems. Every supercomputer will eventually be a hybrid quantum-classical device, drawing on quantum processors to expand what’s possible in scientific research.
The scientists that will become the first power users of quantum-GPU supercomputing already run their simulations and workflows on HPC systems. Chemistry, weather modeling, engineering simulation, and other traditionally HPC-centric fields stand to benefit from quantum acceleration for certain workloads. For these scientists, the QPU is simply another accelerator, alongside the CPUs and GPUs that supercomputing centers already provide.
Making quantum computers readily available, easily programmable, and familiar to access, reserve, and execute at scale is imperative for scientific researchers to be able to adopt quantum processors into workflows. Slurm 26.11 changes that with Hierarchical Resources (HRES) plugins, which allow a site to schedule a QPU as a native, cluster-level resource through a short, portable Lua plugin.

articles.title: Co-Designing Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Inference | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Agentic workloads, long documents, and large codebases are pushing context lengths from tens of thousands of tokens to hundreds of thousands. At those lengths, attention becomes the most expensive part of a transformer layer. Dense attention scores every query against every key, so its cost per query grows with the context length N, and at 128K tokens it can take most of the prefill time in a layer.
The model-level solution is sparse attention, a transformer technique in which each query attends to only a small subset of the context, chosen per query, instead of all of it. This cuts both the compute and the memory traffic of attention on long context.
This post is a practical primer for model developers designing sparse attention that runs well on NVIDIA GPUs. It focuses on model-level sparse attention, where sparsity is trained into the model, rather than drop-in methods applied after training such as BLASST, MInference, or Quest. A production FP8 kernel is used to sweep the indexer’s design knobs (query heads, key heads, head dimension, compression ratio, and speculative-decoding depth), measure how Top-k cost scales, and compare token-level with block-level core attention.
Each section explains what the hardware rewards and why, and ends with a guideline you can apply to your own design. This post follows the same co-design approach as the earlier posts on dense attention and hardware-friendly LLM design.

articles.title: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
articles.summary:
It’s never been easier to steal credentials, thanks to a growing number of phishing kits that give aspiring attackers everything they need in one convenient interface. Some now come with admin dashboards and round-the-clock support, like a SaaS business, and they’re designed specifically to steal Microsoft 365 session tokens.
Even entry-level attackers who replay a stolen token can end up in an active session where the login and MFA are already complete, with instant access to the victim’s cloud resources and email.
Huntress researchers analyzed three of these modern phishing kits. This article breaks down how they capture and replay tokens and what defenders can do about it.
What’s inside a phishing kit
A phishing kit is a pre-packaged set of code and templates, with instructions for launching a phishing campaign and using the data it steals for malicious activity. Basic kits are often simple HTML and script files that spin up a single fake login page.
More advanced kits feature admin dashboards that attackers use to track victims, modify phishing page content, and relay credentials in real time.
To understand why these kits are so dangerous, it helps to look at how they turn phishing lures into usable sessions.

articles.summary:
In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout. The company is now doing something similar with its iconic air-filled soles using its new Tuned Air technology. While previously the level of cushioning in Nike Air shoes was uniform across the entire sole, a new manufacturing process can produce multiple air pockets with varying levels of cushioning and stability.
Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.

A ação cobria compras feitas entre agosto de 2016 e fevereiro de 2026.
A Sony respondeu que a ação, na prática, defendia que terceiros pudessem abrir uma loja no PlayStation e pegar carona nos investimentos da empresa.
O valor pedido oscilou bastante no caminho: £ 5 bilhões em 2022, £ 6,3 bilhões (US$ 7,9 bilhões) em 2023 e, por fim, os £ 2 bilhões (US$ 2,6 bilhões) da estimativa mais recente. Em 2023, a Sony tentou barrar a ação antes do julgamento e não conseguiu.

Avant d’exécuter un fichier téléchargé ou de cliquer sur un lien douteux, il est désormais possible de demander à Claude de lire le rapport VirusTotal et de l’expliquer.

Dans Claude, il est maintenant possible d’ajouter VirusTotal depuis l’annuaire des connecteurs, puis de se connecter avec son compte Google via OAuth. Dans une organisation, un propriétaire peut devoir activer le connecteur au préalable.
Pour un fichier local, Claude calcule son empreinte SHA-256 (un identifiant propre à chaque fichier, obtenu sans l’exécuter) et interroge le rapport associé, car le connecteur n’accède pas aux chemins locaux. Un envoi, une soumission d’URL ou une seconde analyse de domaine ou d’IP n’ont lieu que sur demande explicite.

articles.title: Defect-Aware Chiplet Matching For Heterogeneous Integration Yield (ASU, Ampere)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Arizona State University and Ampere Computing published “DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration.”
Abstract
“Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. The greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP)-based approach provides substantial acceleration, but it does not guarantee yield optimality. Both approaches use a preprocessing pipeline to reduce the problem size. Experimental results on industrial designs demonstrate that, as expected, the ILP-based approach achieves superior solution quality. The GRASP-based approach leads to lower runtimes while still achieving solution quality that is comparable to the ILP-based solution. Together, these methods provide a trade-off …

This is according to NordPass’ latest (and utterly depressing) report on the most popular passwords people use around the world.
The company has once again aggregated all of the passwords criminals leak on the dark web, analyzed them, and tells the world what the most common passwords and phrases are. And year after year, the report shows the same five passwords (or password variant, should we say) being at the very top:

articles.title: A developer got Doom to run on a USB flash drive, and file transfers are the controls
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Doom now runs on a 128GB USB flash drive with its own built-in screen, and players control the game by copying files to the drive or reading files from it. The port is the work of Aaron Christophel, a German embedded software developer and hardware hacker known online as atc1441, whose earlier Doom ports include an electric toothbrush, a Xiaomi Mi Band 10 and a toy video walkie-talkie.
Keeping the whole game on the drive meant working with limited hardware. At the end, Christophel got the USB drive's display chip to handle all of the rendering, input, saves and reloads without any help from the computer it's plugged into.
Christophel says the microcontroller that drives the screen has 128KB of SRAM, 2MB of flash memory, and a measured clock speed of 40MHz. The SRAM is the chip's working memory, where the game has to keep its active state while it runs. The flash has to hold the program code and the game data. With those limits, the original DOS release of Doom was never going to fit.
Instead, Christophel turned to DMC100-DOOM, a stripped-down port by Polish developer Artur Bieniek. Bieniek wrote it for an AC/DC digital clamp meter, a handheld tool electricians use to measure current. The meter's chip has just 32KB of RAM, so Bieniek had the port draw the screen in strips instead of holding a full frame in memory. That focus on squeezing Doom into very little memory made it a natural match for a display controller in a USB stick.

Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
Drought conditions and low reservoir levels are affecting the renewable power source.
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.
Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.
Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases. Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River. And in recent years, the river has seen record-low flows.
Two reservoirs along the Colorado River, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, have struggled to stay above the minimum level required for hydropower plants. At the end of September, Lake Powell’s depth was 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines that produce electricity at the Glen Canyon power plant. Im deutschsprachigen Raum besser bekannt als Walter. Es gibt unzählige Bücher mit Wimmelbildern, in denen die simple Frage „Wo ist Walter?“ das Konzept auf den Punkt bringt. Artificial Intelligence
Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams
Companies build agentic AI platforms to govern the applications, tools, skills, models, and storage that agents use. The nondeterministic nature of generative AI models introduces a complexity that previous software development practices didn’t anticipate. Consider a real estate app that generates property listings from retrieved data: does it accurately reflect the property, or hallucinate features that don’t exist? Or a customer service agent grounded on internal knowledge bases: can you verify that it doesn’t surface confidential information?
Until recently, responsible AI (RAI) was model-centric, scoped to the machine learning development lifecycle: training, testing, and inference. Models didn’t reason, use tools, or take actions. When the conversation extended to model-powered systems, it covered statistically bounded situations you could test against known inputs. Generative AI powered applications and agents changed this. The systems now reason, act, compose tools dynamically, and interact over multiple steps, expanding both the scope and the depth of what responsible AI must cover.

articles.title: Pretxt Emerges Stealth With $5M Seed and an AI Supervision Tool
articles.summary:
Pretxt, with offices in Aspen, CO, and Dublin, Ireland, has emerged from stealth with $5 million seed funding raised from Deciens Capital, Howdy Partners and Service Provider Capital. Pretxt enters the emerging category of firms providing technology to prevent AI agents escaping their guardrails and causing unintended harm.
AI is more like a person than like traditional computer code: it doesn’t simply run; it receives, interprets, misinterprets and responds to ambiguous instructions. It is the combination of misinterpretation and wide agency of response that results in AI agents going rogue and potentially causing harm.
Since it is impossible to categorically exclude ambiguity in language (which is how we instruct the agents), our only alternative method of controlling them is to limit their agency. But too stringent a limitation of agency could become an unacceptable restriction on a potentially huge business benefit.
So, without a new category of supervision control, it is likely that we cannot have beneficial AI agents without also having potentially dangerous rogue agents. This requirement for a new control is leading to the emergence of a type of cybersecurity product that attempts to recognize a potentially harmful agentic action at runtime and control it before it can cause harm.

When Stephanie Ohumu’s grandmother died in 2023, she took with her recipes the family could no longer recreate, words Ohumu relied on her to explain, and cultural knowledge that had never been written down.
“It used to be that if I encountered Edo words in the wild, I’d text my grandma or call her and she would translate for me,” Ohumu said. “Not just that, there are meals we cannot make the way we grew up eating them because they were never written down and we don’t know how to make them. All of that went away.”
Her grandmother’s death made Ohumu, a journalist and artificial intelligence expert, realise how much Edo culture existed only in the memories of older people, with little preserved for future generations. “Language is a repository of knowledge. It took my grandmother dying for me to really understand that,” she said.
The loss also raised questions about how languages like Edo, a language spoken by an estimated 2 million people across seven local government areas in Edo State, southwestern Nigeria, would survive in an increasingly digital world. Ohumu worried that the lack of reliable digital material would leave such languages poorly represented in artificial intelligence (AI) systems, increasing the risk of convincing but inaccurate translations and responses.

articles.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
articles.summary:
A Lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform allowed researchers to take control of Kokoro, a text-to-speech model used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services.
An attacker hijacking the account could use it as a distribution channel in supply-chain attacks, potentially leading to data theft or code execution.
However, the researchers demonstrated a stealthier attack: they modified the model's weights so it produced audio that differed from the input text, without changing the underlying application code.
Because only the weights change, there is no malicious code or signature for malware scanners to detect, the researchers say.
"We changed what this model says by fine-tuning its neural weights. Same input text. Same voice file. Same configuration. Same inference code — not a single line touched in the application that runs it," said security researcher Alon Hertz.
Kokoro is an open-weight model that converts text into speech. It supports multiple languages and has more than 50 voice presets.
Although its developer, Hexgrad, has not pushed an update since April 2025, the project continues to be popular, with nearly 13 million monthly downloads on Hugging Face. The GitHub repository and the Python package on PyPI also went silent around the same time.
Kokoro is supported by developer tools from Google, NVIDIA, and Intel, including software for voice agents and on-device speech synthesis. AMD and Amazon Web Services have also publis…

Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.
The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge.
It’s “worse than a bug”

articles.title: Just 403 data centers use as much electricity as the whole state of Michigan does in a year
articles.summary:
The big picture: Michigan is home to about 10 million people and a big chunk of America's auto industry. Yet a new study estimates that a few hundred data centers scattered across the US used about as much electricity in a single year as that entire state. Strangely, no federal or state agency actually tracks that number, so researchers had to build their own list of these facilities, partly from satellite imagery.
The research, published on Monday in Nature Sustainability, comes from a Harvard-led team. It focuses only on hyperscale data centers – the largest class of facility, mostly run by cloud and AI giants. Operators and utilities aren't required to disclose how much power individual sites draw, so the team combined industry data with satellite checks to compile 403 facilities, then estimated what each consumed between May 2024 and April 2025.
Depending on how hard those sites were assumed to run, their combined usage landed somewhere between 68 and 99 terawatt-hours. The middle estimate of about 82 TWh works out to roughly 1.8% of all US electricity consumption. That upper figure, for comparison, is about what Michigan, Indiana or Tennessee each go through in a year.
Much of that load sits in Virginia. The state's 142 facilities alone use roughly a quarter of the total. Add Oregon, Ohio and Iowa, and those four states account for about half.

articles.title: Une panne frappe NSA Net, le réseau ultra-secret du renseignement américain : voici ce que l’on sait
articles.summary:
Mardi 17 novembre 2026, CNN a révélé que le réseau sur lequel les employés de la National Security Agency (NSA) échangent des informations classifiées ne fonctionne plus.
La chaîne américaine dit s’appuyer sur six personnes au fait de la situation. La journaliste Natasha Bertrand, qui signe l’enquête avec quatre collègues, en évoquait cinq dans le premier message publié sur X.
L’agence de renseignement, dont le siège se trouve à Fort Meade, dans le Maryland, n’avait pas encore répondu aux questions de CNN au moment de la publication.
Un réseau réservé aux échanges classifiés
Ce réseau, baptisé NSA Net, n’a rien à voir avec le site public de l’agence. Il sert aux agents à faire circuler des informations classifiées en interne, c’est-à-dire des contenus qui ne peuvent pas passer par une messagerie ou un réseau ordinaire. Sa panne bloque donc ces échanges au sein de l’agence.
On ignore pour l’instant depuis quand la panne dure, combien de services sont touchés et quand le réseau pourra être rétabli. Selon les sources de CNN, l’agence a mis en place des arrivées échelonnées pour son personnel le temps de comprendre ce qui se passe.
Sur la cause, les sources de CNN affirment qu’il n’existe « à ce stade » aucune preuve d’une cyberattaque.

Côté gaz, le prix repère de vente, qui sert de référence depuis la fin des tarifs réglementés en 2023, a encore augmenté de 6,6 % au 1er novembre 2026, après plusieurs mois de hausse.

Le principe est simple : rassembler un maximum de consommateurs pour négocier une offre commune auprès des fournisseurs, chacun signant ensuite son propre contrat. L’idée avait été lancée par l’UFC-Que Choisir en 2013, à travers l’opération « Gaz moins cher ensemble ». Le fournisseur retenu, Lampiris, avait alors accordé à 71 000 foyers une remise de 13 % TTC sur le prix du kWh de gaz par rapport au tarif réglementé de l’époque.

Depuis, le modèle a été repris par d’autres associations de consommateurs, par des courtiers en énergie et même par des collectivités. Depuis début septembre, les exemples d’achats groupés se multiplient dans l’actualité.

Some AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other leading AI labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes — even if they include civilians or locations like schools — simply by being told they’re playing a game, according to a new research report by Vals.
Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a combination of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see if the AI models would mark targets in drone and satellite imagery.
The models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other companies frequently identified potential targets in drone and satellite imagery, including civilians and surrendering soldiers. When the models refused to cooperate, researchers were able to jailbreak them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game.
The findings come amid growing fears about the immediate risks posed by AI, beyond the existential threats associated with artificial general intelligence.

articles.title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
articles.summary:
Qwik, the resumable JavaScript framework originally created at Builder.io, has released its 2.0 Release Candidate, targeting a rewrite of how the framework encodes resumable state in server-rendered HTML and introducing experimental out-of-order streaming. The RC was published on 1st October 2026 as @qwik.dev/core@2.0.0-rc.0, around two years and eight months after the initial Towards Qwik 2.0 design article.
In v1, Qwik propagated state updates by sprinkling HTML comment markers such as <!--qv--> and <!--t=8--> throughout the rendered body to flag component boundaries and the text nodes a signal should update. That approach forced a single ordered write pass, added CPU and memory overhead, and made out-of-order streaming impossible because a slow fetch blocked everything after it. In v2 the comments are gone, with state and virtual node information instead compressed into two <script type="qwik/state"> and <script type="qwik/vnode"> blocks at the end of the document.
On Qwik's internal runs of js-framework-benchmark, v2 posts a weighted geometric mean of 1.23 times slower than vanilla JavaScript, ahead of Vue 3.5 at 1.25x, Angular 22 at 1.42x, React 19 with the compiler at 1.53x, and v1 itself at 2.59x. A detailed classmethod walkthrough that built the same starter against both versions reported server-rendered HTML went from 60 comments to zero, with JavaScript required before interactivity dropping from 59KB to 9KB, though total bundle size grew.

To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. Costco, la cadena estadounidense en la que sólo se compra con tarjeta de socio, prepara su tercera tienda en la Comunidad de Madrid, concretamente en Torrejón de Ardoz. Con este movimiento, la cadena parece seguir adelante con su expansión en nuestro país.
Suelo e inversión. Costco Wholesale Corporation ha cerrado, a través de su filial en España, la compra de unos 60.000 metros cuadrados de suelo en Torrejón, con una inversión aproximada de 80 millones de euros, cifra cubre toda la apertura y no sólo el terreno.
Cómo será la tienda. Tendrá unos 15.000 metros cuadrados y gasolinera propia, y abriría en septiembre de 2027. Para comprar dentro habrá que ser socio, porque Costco funciona como un club de precios al que se accede pagando una cuota anual. Vamos, que sin tarjeta no se pasa por caja. Y vende la mayoría de sus productos en formatos extragrandes o packs familiares para mover volumen y ajustar precios.
El mapa en España. Con Torrejón, la cadena tendría tres tiendas en la región, junto a las de Getafe y Las Rozas. Fuera de Madrid suma otras tres, en Sevilla, Sestao (Vizcaya) y Zaragoza, además de un almacén logístico en Torija (Guadalajara), datos que recoge la agencia.
La apertura encaja en la estrategia de crecimiento de la multinacional en España, aunque la fecha no es definitiva. Habrá que ver si la licencia municipal llega a tiempo, porque de ella depende ese plazo.

articles.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
articles.summary:
The Fugaku supercomputer operated by Japan's RIKEN Center for Computational Science has been taken offline following a security breach.
The organization says that between November 10 and 13, an unauthorized party exploited the public dashboard displaying Fugaku's operational status to gain access to multiple internal servers.
Although the research center has yet to determine the access method, RIKEN’s investigation confirmed that the intruder accessed some servers to plant malware that targeted user data.
Specifically, the organization says that the following details have been compromised:
- Names, email addresses, and user IDs of 4,222 Fugaku users
- Names and email addresses of 375 Rikyu users
- SSH private keys and access keys stored on users’ computers
- Research data files stored on users’ computers
RIKEN notes that the attacker used some of the access keys in attempts to connect to additional systems, but the investigation did not determine further unauthorized access or theft of research results.
The organization has not attributed the attack, and it’s still working to determine the exact intrusion method.
RIKEN’s Center for Computational Science operates the two supercomputers, making them available to researchers in academia and industry sectors.

“If money is increasingly digital, why should access to that money completely depend on a functioning network, a smartphone, a remote server or a particular digital channel at the exact moment someone needs to transact?” said Segun Ademigoke, the startup’s founder and CEO.
At the heart of the ecosystem is the Tratum Node, a secure physical financial endpoint that combines secure hardware, cryptographic device identity, local transaction state and communication capabilities. Under rules set by the institution, a Node can carry out approved transactions locally, record them cryptographically, and then synchronise and reconcile with the bank’s systems once connectivity returns.

articles.title: Cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images are stolen within seconds
articles.summary:
Credentials and access secrets exposed in public Docker Hub images are being extracted and exploited by attackers within as little as eight seconds of publication.
Two researchers at Stony Brook University, Billy Tsouvalas and Nick Nikiforakis, measured the extraction speed by publishing a total of 300 honeypot images across eight public container registries.
Over a period of four months, the researchers exposed AWS, OpenAI, and Anthropic API keys, along with decoy SSH and database credentials.
They then monitored the use of these keys and placed detection tools to notify them when the images were built, ran, or had a shell opened.
The two researchers presented the experiment and the resulting findings yesterday at the ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS).
They noted that their images were pulled more than 75,000 times, and the planted AWS keys received over 140,000 API calls from 5,000 unique IP addresses.
The AWS traffic showed a broad pattern, from checking whether the keys worked to listing available resources, and sometimes proceeding to consume them.
The fastest observed use of a planted AWS key came 7.86 seconds after the image was published on Docker Hub. The median time for the first API call was 51.19 seconds, while all 100 AWS keys were used within 15 minutes.
The exposed OpenAI and Anthropic keys were quickly hijacked to exhaust the test-account balances.

South African crypto platform OVEX has gone live with a custom AI fraud detection system, built by machine learning consultancy DataProphet, that catches 98 per cent of fraudsters in testing.
Founded in 2017, OVEX offers South Africa’s largest selection of digital asset markets, and has partnered with several leading cryptocurrency companies and firms, including Invictus Capital, Hyperion, and TrueUSD.
DataProphet, meanwhile, was formed in 2014, and builds and runs custom machine learning for financial services, manufacturing, and other businesses. The two companies began working together back in April to replace OVEX’s rules-based fraud system with AI that learns how fraudsters behave.
Rather than judging an account from a snapshot, the system reads a user’s full activity history in sequence, including every login, deposit, trade and withdrawal. Two models, one trained on fraudulent behaviour and one on honest customers, assess which pattern each account more closely resembles. Accounts that lean towards the fraud model are flagged for investigation.
By late July, the model was catching 98 per cent of fraudsters in testing, compared with 75 per cent for the old system, and flagged 100 per cent of fraud cases it had never seen before. OVEX expects 99 per cent fewer false alarms and a 92 per cent reduction in undetected fraud. The platform also includes a tool showing investigators when an account’s behaviour turned suspicious, and a dashboard for retraining models.

Jusqu'ici, Windows 11 27H2 avait fait parler de lui à travers les indiscrétions de journalistes bien renseignés, mais la prochaine version annuelle du système commence à laisser des traces plus concrètes. Le chercheur XenoPanther vient en effet de découvrir une référence explicite à 27H2 dans la toute dernière build expérimentale de Windows 11, publiée le 13 novembre. Une première qui donne un peu plus de consistance aux projets prêtés à Microsoft pour 2027.
Une référence à Windows 11 27H2 cachée dans les stratégies de groupe
C’est donc en fouillant les fichiers de la build 29708.1003 distribuée sur le canal expérimental Future Platforms, que XenoPanther a repéré une entrée baptisée SUPPORTED_Windows_11_27H2, accompagnée du libellé « Windows 11, version 27H2 or later ».
La référence figure dans le fichier Windows.adml, qui contient les textes utilisés par les modèles d’administration de Windows. Ces fichiers permettent aux équipes informatiques de gérer les stratégies de groupe, et servent entre autres à indiquer les versions minimales du système nécessaires pour appliquer une stratégie donnée.

Hyperscale data centers, in this case, refer to sites run by a hyperscale cloud or content provider, or a colocation operator who serves one, with a capacity in the tens of megawatts. The 675 candidate sites came from data vendor Baxtel, with 403 confirmed with satellite imagery and building-footprint maps, at an average capacity of 39.9 MW and a median of 36 MW.
Nobody officially counts what the data centers actually draw from the grid. Instead, the electricity is estimated by multiplying each site’s maximum capacity by the hours in a year and an estimate of how hard the data centers run. The Rubin HPC chip was announced this week at the Supercomputing 2026 conference as a new part of Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, but it's not expected until 2028, and the company has yet to release several specs that HPC buyers care about most.
The core count offers the first clue to what Nvidia is building. The current Rubin GPU has 224 streaming multiprocessors and 28,672 CUDA cores, so getting past 50,000 would take at least 74% more cores.
That suggests Rubin HPC may spread its cores across several dies in one package, as the two-die Rubin does, or as the four-die Rubin Ultra that Nvidia originally planned, a design since reportedly scaled back. Nvidia has not confirmed the chip's physical layout and describes the core count only as being "on a single GPU." The image it released with the announcement does not appear to show a multi-die design.
Nvidia's pitch is less about raw compute and more about keeping that compute busy. The company says climate modeling, engineering simulation, genomic analysis and financial risk work tend to follow the same pattern: a program reaches into a huge dataset, pulls out a few scattered values, runs a calculation and then repeats that step an enormous number of times. articles.title: Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Across Latin America, India, and Southeast Asia, WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging applications. That makes it an obvious place to build an AI agent. For many end users, it is how they expect to interact with businesses. However, it is also a genuinely difficult surface to build for, even when your agent already runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
The agent is rarely the hard part. The integration is. Inbound messages arrive as deeply nested, type-dependent payloads that must be authenticated and normalized before your agent can read them. Media such as voice notes, images, and documents each require their own processing pipeline. Beyond message handling, you need conversation memory that survives sessions, durable schedules for reminders, and an authenticated path for external systems to trigger outbound messages. And anything you send more than 24 hours after the end user’s last message must use a pre-approved Meta message template.
Wiring that up means configuring more than 10 AWS services and learning a set of WhatsApp system behaviors that most teams discover only by hitting them. None of it is visible to a customer, but all of it has to work. Most teams either build it from scratch or hand the integration to a third-party service.
SMART (Social Messaging Agent Runtime Toolkit) is a third option: an open source Python SDK and Terraform stack that gives you the full channel layer.…

Decision models are LLMs that don’t produce output tokens; instead, they’re tuned to use their general intelligence to quickly and cheaply decide between preset options, while registering its level of confidence in the choice. They’re useful in production environments, where fast decisions can be more important than the reasoning provided by a slower and more expensive frontier model.
TypeSafe became a $7.5 billion company after releasing its Jev family of models, which continues to dominate usage (at least where we can see metrics from services like OpenRouter, which handled more than 1.5 billion queries to TypeSafe’s models last week).
However, it’s easy to make a decision model, and dozens were released in the wake of Jev. One Amazon engineer made one in a weekend, and soon every hyperscaler had its own option. On Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that his company is rolling out its decision model, Microsoft-Decision-1.1, for wide use on Azure immediately.

Apple's own setup screen is surprisingly blunt about the trade-off, warning that the feature "isn't as secure as Touch ID or Face ID." As a result, the feature only gets you past the lock screen. Apple Pay, saved passwords and app sign-ins all still need a fingerprint. articles.title: El Código Civil permite a los propietarios arrancar las ramas y las raíces de los árboles y plantas de su vecino en estos casos
articles.summary:
Los árboles y plantas pueden ser objeto de conflicto entre vecinos si sobrepasan el límite de la parcela en que han sido plantados.
Por un lado están las ramas que sobresalen en el jardín de nuestro vecino y, por otro, están las raíces que atraviesan el terreno de la otra persona.
El Código Civil prevé que el afectado pueda reclamar el corte de las ramas (artículo 592). También tenemos el derecho a realizar nosotros mismos el corte de las raíces, pero solo en nuestro terreno.
Qué distancia deben guardar los árboles
Antes de llegar a este problema, el Código Civil (artículo 591) prevé cómo deben ser plantados los árboles en los límites de otras fincas.
En primer lugar, se aplicará la distancia que establezcan las ordenanzas o costumbres locales. En caso contrario, habrá que dejar un margen de dos metros de distancia de la línea divisoria (para árboles altos) o 50 centímetros (arbustos o árboles bajos).
El propietario tiene derecho a solicitar que sean arrancados los árboles que se planten a menos distancia de su finca de la permitida. No hay derecho a arrancarlos por nuestra cuenta.
El derecho de corte de raíces solo llega hasta el límite de nuestra finca. No podemos pasar al terreno del vecino.
Los derechos anteriores son respecto de fincas colindantes. No pueden confundirse con el derecho a actuar sobre plantas situadas en zonas comunes de una comunidad de propietarios. También puede haber otros conflictos en las zonas comunes.

Por su parte, las plataformas piratas suelen ofrecer sus propias aplicaciones mediante enlaces de descarga en sitios alternativos. Al instalar esos archivos, el usuario incorpora un programa que no pasó por los mismos filtros.

A malware attack reportedly used Optimizely scripts on 178 organisation websites, including Zoom, Salesforce and IKEA, to target card details and crypto wallet addresses.
You may trust the website you are visiting. But what about the tools running behind it?
Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a malware campaign involving websites linked to 178 organisations worldwide, including Zoom, Salesforce, IKEA, HSBC and Crocs. The attack shows how a compromised third-party tool can turn familiar websites into potential entry points for cybercriminals.
According to findings, the malicious code was injected through Optimizely Web, a platform companies use to run website experiments and A/B testing. This technique allows brands to show different versions of a webpage and measure how users respond.
The attack exploited that routine website function to deliver code capable of interfering with what users entered or copied on affected pages.
How a trusted website tool became a malware route
The attacker reportedly exploited a feature in Optimizely that allows customers to add JavaScript to projects. JavaScript is commonly used to make websites interactive and run features within a browser.
Malicious JavaScript was added to customer projects and delivered through Optimizely's trusted domain. This made the activity harder to identify as suspicious because the code came from a service already used by the affected websites.

Artificial Intelligence
Secure OAuth patterns for Snowflake Cortex AI through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Enterprises today need a clear way to extend their authentication and authorization controls into the agentic layer, often requiring either broad service account permissions or custom-built auth integrations that add operational overhead. When an AI agent running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model) needs to call the Snowflake-managed MCP server (which exposes Snowflake Cortex Agents as one of its tool types) through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the first question enterprises must answer is: how does the agent authenticate? In this post, we walk through three Open Authorization (OAuth) configurations we tested on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Snowflake OAuth (per-user, no external Identity Provider, or IdP), three-legged OAuth with a third-party Identity Provider (corporate single sign-on, or SSO), and two-legged OAuth with a third-party Identity Provider (shared service user). Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity also supports an on-behalf-of (OBO) grant (TOKEN_EXCHANGE) that delivers per-user identity for unattended workloads without a consent prompt. We focus on the three configurations we tested end-to-end, flagging where OBO fits as we go. By the end, you will be able to identify which pattern suits your enterprise scenario.
